paragraphs: A rubber tracked dumper exists for ground too soft to carry a wheeled truck. The tracks spread the load so it can work a marsh, a forest floor or a fresh construction site without sinking, and the body sits low and wide over them. That combination gives the machine a squat, deliberate look unlike any road vehicle.
The mesh runs 457,885 polygons and 241,813 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the track links, the tipping body and the cab.

This page is unusually deep, with seven other builds from $99 to $159 including dirty, old and orange variants and rigged versions prepared for Maya and Cinema 4D. Aimed at construction, forestry and utilities visualisation, equipment marketing, site scenes and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2024.

A modern coupe lives on its shoulder line and its roof taper, and black is the paint that tests both hardest: every reflection runs unbroken down the flank, and any flaw in the surfacing shows as a kink in that reflection. This build carries the low nose, the fastback roof and the wide rear track that define the shape.

The mesh is efficient at 128,312 polygons and 138,083 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, a sensible economy on a symmetrical body, and the build is simplified in the interior rather than the exterior, which is the right saving for a car usually shown from outside.
At $99 and built to StemCell specification, it suits automotive marketing and configurators, urban and traffic visualisation, showroom renders, advertising and games. On sale since 2026.

An air launched hypersonic weapon is mostly booster. A rocket stage accelerates the vehicle to speed, then a wedge shaped glide body separates and flies the rest of the way unpowered. That two part arrangement gives the missile its unusual profile: a long cylinder with a shrouded nose that does not taper the way a conventional missile does.
The mesh is efficient at 63,437 polygons and 63,757 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the fins, the shroud and the pylon lugs.

At $99 it suits defence and strategic visualisation, news and documentary graphics, aviation renders where an aircraft carries stores, education material and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it hangs correctly from a pylon. On sale since 2022.

A full teardown is only useful if every part is its own object. Display assembly, battery, logic board, camera module, taptic engine, shields, brackets and screws all exist separately here, which is what allows an exploded layout, a flat lay for a teardown spread, or an animation that puts the phone back together.

The mesh runs 325,384 polygons and 168,857 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density concentrated in the camera assembly and the connector housings where a macro camera lands.

At $99 and built to StemCell specification, it suits repair and service documentation, technology journalism and teardown content, product and engineering marketing, teaching material and games. On sale since 2023.

A road line striper is a walk-behind or ride-on machine with a paint reservoir, a pump, an adjustable spray gun on an arm and a guide wheel out front so the operator can follow a chalk line. The gun position and the guide are what make it recognisable, because everything else looks like a large mower.
The mesh runs 131,434 polygons and 135,081 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and it arrives rigged so the wheels turn and the spray arm can be positioned.

At $99 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits road maintenance and municipal visualisation, car park and airfield marking scenes, equipment marketing and catalogues, training material and games. On sale since 2024.

A truck mounted drilling rig folds its mast down for the road and raises it on site, which is the single fact that shapes the whole machine: the mast pivots at the rear, hydraulic rams lift it, and jacks take the weight off the suspension before drilling starts. This build shows the rig set up and working.
The mesh is efficient at 116,420 polygons and 133,339 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the mast lattice, the drawworks and the jack assemblies.

At $99 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits oil, gas and geological exploration visualisation, mining and water well presentation, equipment marketing, site scenes and games. On sale since 2025.

A pump jack is a machine that explains itself: a counterweighted beam rocking on an A-frame, driven by a belt from a small motor, lifting a rod string up and down a well. Everyone recognises the nodding motion, and the whole visual identity of onshore oil production rests on it.

The mesh runs 284,241 polygons and 300,037 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 21 texture maps carrying the paint, the rust and the oil staining that these machines wear within a season.

This page carries a generic variant at $99 and rigged builds at $119, which are the ones to take if the beam has to nod. The static model at $99 covers oil and gas visualisation, energy sector marketing, rural and industrial landscapes, documentary work and games. On sale since 2015.

The counterweight is the clever part of a pump jack. It stores energy on the downstroke and gives it back on the up, so a small motor can lift a rod string weighing tonnes. That is why the beam carries such a heavy crank weight at the back, and why the machine rocks at a slow steady rhythm rather than working in bursts.
The mesh runs 284,255 polygons and 300,037 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the detail in the crank, the bearings and the walking beam.

Three rigged builds share this page at $119, including versions prepared for Maya and for Cinema 4D. The static model at $99 covers oil and gas visualisation, energy marketing, industrial landscapes, documentary work and games. On sale since 2023.

The crest is what everyone knows this dinosaur for, and its shape matters: a long hollow tube curving back from the skull, connected to the nasal passages, which is why the leading theory is that the animal used it to make sound. Getting the curve and the attachment right is the whole identification.

The mesh is 78,724 polygons and 80,133 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 19 texture maps - 9 at 8192x8192 and 10 at 2048x2048. Nine maps at the largest size is what a skin covered in fine scale detail needs.
At $99 it suits palaeontology and natural history material, museum and exhibition displays, documentary work, children's education content, film and television, and games. On sale since 2016.

A trading desk is defined by its monitor arrangement: several screens on articulated arms, banked in two rows so the operator can see all of them without turning, with cable management running down the back of the mount. That wall of displays is what says finance rather than office, and it has to be arranged correctly to read.
The mesh runs 226,761 polygons and 233,923 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, with the screens as separate surfaces so charts or interfaces can be applied without masking.

At $99 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits financial and corporate interior visualisation, fintech and trading platform marketing, office furniture retail renders, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2026.

The American school bus is one of the most standardised vehicles anywhere: the colour, the black rub rails, the stop arm, the crossing gate at the front bumper and the flashing lights are all mandated. That regulation is why the vehicle is instantly recognisable in silhouette and why any deviation looks wrong.

The mesh runs 174,061 polygons and 181,103 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096, carrying the lettering, the rub rails and the road grime.

A rigged build sits on this page at $129 for when the wheels turn and the door opens. The static model at $99 covers urban and suburban visualisation, education and child safety material, film and television, advertising and games. On sale since 2015.

The Cherokee is the low wing counterpart to the high wing trainers, and the difference is immediately visible: the wing sits under the cabin, there is a single door on the starboard side, and the wing itself has a constant chord that gives it a distinctly rectangular planform. Thousands of pilots learned on this shape.

The mesh is efficient at 47,445 polygons and 49,525 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits an aircraft usually shown on an apron or in a circuit rather than in extreme close-up.
At $99 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits general aviation visualisation, flight school and club material, airfield scenes, aviation advertising and games. On sale since 2024.

A frog is a rigging problem disguised as a simple animal. The hind legs fold into a deep Z that has to straighten explosively for a jump, the throat inflates and deflates independently of the body, and the whole spine is short and stiff. A rig built on a generic quadruped will not produce any of that.
This build arrives rigged and prepared for Blender, which means the leg articulation and the throat deformation are already solved in the application the animation will happen in.
At $99 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits wildlife documentary and education, biology and ecology material, children's content, advertising, animation and games. On sale since 2026.

The Model Y shares most of its parts with the saloon below it but raises the roof and the ride height, which changes the proportions completely: a taller glasshouse, a hatchback tail and a longer rear overhang. Those differences are subtle on paper and obvious in silhouette, which is exactly why they have to be right.
The mesh is efficient at 107,776 polygons and 121,063 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 9 texture maps - 7 at 4096x4096 and 2 at 2048x2048.

This page is well stocked, with blue, silver and standard builds at $129 and rigged versions at $149 including builds prepared for Maya and Cinema. This simple interior model at $99 suits urban visualisation, background traffic, advertising and games. On sale since 2019.
